{{Short description|Russian astronomer}}
'''Georgij Albertovich Krasinsky''' (Георгий Альбертович Красинский, February 19, 1939; [[Leningrad]], [[USSR]] – March 17, 2011, [[Saint Petersburg]]) was a Russian [[astronomer]] active at the [[Institute of Applied Astronomy]],  [[Russian Academy of Science]], [[St Petersburg]].<ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=http://www.ipa.nw.ru/kradead.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120804182225/http://www.ipa.nw.ru/kradead.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 August 2012 |title=Obituary |publisher=[[Institute of Applied Astronomy]] |language=Russian |accessdate=19 January 2012 }}</ref> He was notable for research on planetary motions and [[ephemeris|ephemerides]].

Krasinsky graduated in 1961 from the Faculty of Mathematics and Mechanics  of [[Leningrad State University]].  He then became a graduate student and, subsequently, an employee of the Институт теоретической астрономии АН СССР (Institute of [[Theoretical astronomy|Theoretical Astronomy]], [[Academy of Sciences of the USSR]]). In 1965 he successfully defended his thesis for the Russian [[Candidate of Science]] degree (Ph.D.) in physical and mathematical sciences. In 1988 he was transferred to the Institute of Applied Astronomy of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR. There in 1989 he completed his dissertation for the Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree<ref name=obit/> (similar to [[habilitation]]). Krasinsky and colleagues developed and implemented a problem-oriented language SLON and a software system (called the ERA system) for solving problems in dynamic and ephemeris astronomy. (ERA is the acronym for "Ephemerides for Research in Astronomy".)<ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-94-009-0985-4_37|chapter=Problem Oriented Language for Ephemeris Astronomy and Its Realisation in the System ERA|title=Applications of Computer Technology to Dynamical Astronomy|year=1989|last1=Krasinsky|first1=G. A.|last2=Novikov|first2=F. A.|last3=Scripnichenko|first3=V. I.|pages=219–229|isbn=978-94-010-6932-8|s2cid=123340575 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1017/S0252921100046613|title=ERA: Knowledge Base for Ephemeris and Dynamical Astronomy|year=1997|last1=Krasinsky|first1=G. A.|last2=Vasilyev|first2=M.V.|journal=International Astronomical Union Colloquium|volume=165|pages=239–244|bibcode=1997dana.coll..239K|doi-access=free}}</ref> Krasinsky and colleagues applied the ERA software system to develop a high-precision, long-term numerical theory of the motions of our solar system's planets and Earth's moon.<ref name=obit/><ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-94-011-5534-2_29|chapter=Analysis of LLR Data by the Program System Era|title=Dynamics and Astrometry of Natural and Artificial Celestial Bodies|year=1997|last1=Aleshkina|first1=E.Yu.|last2=Krasinsky|first2=G. A.|last3=Vasilyev|first3=M. V.|pages=227–232|isbn=978-94-010-6330-2}}</ref>

Krasinsky was the president of [[International Astronomical Union|IAU]] commission 4-DI on ephemerides during 2003-2006.

The [[asteroid]] [[5714 Krasinsky]] is named after him. Krasinsky was awarded in 1980 the [[Order of the Badge of Honour]] and in 1982 the [[USSR State Prize]]. He made important contributions to the theory and implementation of Russia's radio interferometric complex "Kvazar-KVO" created at the Институт прикладной астрономии (Institute of Applied Astronomy) of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS). For his contribution to the creation of the complex, Krasinsky in 2002 was awarded the [[Order of Honour (Russia)|Order of Honour]].<ref name=obit/>

His students include [[Elena V. Pitjeva]].
